title: Exploring Quantum Phase Transitions Beyond Landau Theory on a Quantum Processor
authors: Ruizhe Shen, Yin Zhong, Ching Hua Lee
abstract: Direct continuous quantum phase transitions between phases that break distinct symmetries challenge the conventional Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm and provide a framework for deconfined quantum criticality. Here, we investigate a Landau-forbidden ferromagnetic-to-valence-bond-solid (FM-VBS) transition in a frustrated one-dimensional spin chain using superconducting quantum processors. Combining matrix-product-state-assisted circuit preparation with quantum-hardware measurements, we resolve the suppression of long-range ferromagnetic correlations and the redistribution of competing-order fluctuations across the transition. Distance-resolved correlations and finite-size analyses reveal signatures consistent with critical behavior. We further extend our investigation to nonequilibrium dynamics, directly preparing dimerized states and tracking the evolution of VBS order and joint FM-VBS fluctuations under local unitary interactions. Our results establish a versatile quantum-hardware framework for probing competing orders, critical correlations, and many-body dynamics beyond conventional Landau theory.
summary: This work explores quantum phase transitions between competing magnetic orders (FM and VBS) that defy conventional Landau theory. By utilizing superconducting quantum processors, the authors simulate the transition dynamics, confirming the suppression of long-range FM order and the emergence of VBS correlations. This establishes a versatile quantum-hardware platform for probing complex critical phenomena.
main_problem: The paper investigates continuous quantum phase transitions (QPTs) that challenge the Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm, specifically focusing on direct transitions between phases with distinct symmetries.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated the signatures of a direct continuous Ferromagnetic-to-Valence-Bond-Solid (FM-VBS) transition using both theoretical simulations and superconducting quantum hardware measurements.
method: The study combines theoretical tools like DMRG with quantum hardware protocols, employing tensor-network-assisted circuit preparation to simulate ground states and non-equilibrium dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a frustrated one-dimensional spin-1/2 XZ chain governed by a Hamiltonian involving nearest and next-nearest-neighbor couplings, studied across a frustration strength K.
key_observables: Long-distance ferromagnetic correlators ($C_{	ext{long}}^{zz}$), staggered VBS order parameter ($O_{	ext{VBS}}$), and the second-moment correlation length ($\xi_{2	ext{nd}}$).
important_parameters: The frustration strength K, with critical regimes identified near $K_c \approx 0.4$.
main_assumptions: The quantum hardware simulation relies on approximating DMRG states via parameterized quantum circuits and uses finite-size scaling analysis to infer critical behavior.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the suppression of FM correlations and growth of VBS order across the transition (Fig. 1), and compare hardware measurements of correlators and joint probability distributions against DMRG results (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework of Landau-forbidden transitions, to detailing the quantum hardware protocol for state preparation, and finally presenting results on both equilibrium critical signatures and non-equilibrium dynamics.
why_interesting: The combination of simulating unconventional QPTs (like deconfined criticality) on near-term quantum hardware provides a crucial testbed for many-body physics beyond standard theoretical models.
